data.one_liner: Flutter health SDK for iOS HealthKit and Android Health Connect integration.
data.what_it_does: Provides an interface to read, write, delete, update, aggregate, and synchronize health and fitness data across iOS and Android health platforms. Offers type safety for typed health data types.
use_when: You need to integrate Apple HealthKit in an iOS app.
You need to integrate Android Health Connect in an Android app.
Your app requires reading or writing typed health records such as steps, heart rate, or sleep.
avoid_when: Your app does not require health or fitness data integration.
You require cross-platform health user profile features that must work identically on Android (which does not provide a user health profile API here).
strengths: Supports 143 typed health data types with compile-time type safety.
Handles incremental data synchronization and privacy-first architecture.
Covers both iOS HealthKit and Android Health Connect natively.
weaknesses: Requires manual platform configuration on both Android (Manifest changes, custom MainActivity, Gradle settings) and iOS (Capabilities, Info.plist usage descriptions).
Some features like user characteristic reads are restricted to iOS.
data.setup_notes: Requires setting minimum SDK versions, enabling AndroidX and Jetifier, configuring compileSdkExtension 19, updating AndroidManifest.xml and MainActivity, plus enabling HealthKit capability and adding usage descriptions in iOS Info.plist.
